chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, who said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Mukhariqi al-Kufi, from Abi Junadah al-Saluli, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever fasts in the month of Shaban, it will be for him a purification from every slip, oath, and haste. Abi Hamzah said: I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the 'wasmah' (oath)? He replied: The oath in disobedience and the vow in disobedience. I asked: Then what is the 'badirah' (haste)? He replied: The oath taken in anger, and repenting from it and regretting it.

key_terms.الْبَادِرَه: Haste or impulsiveness, specifically regarding oaths in anger
key_terms.شَعْبَان: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of fasting in Shaban and what does it purify one from?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), highlighting the month of Shaban as a preparatory period for Ramadan by purifying the soul from specific behavioral defects. The Imam clarifies that 'wasmah' refers to oaths or vows made in the context of sin, while 'badirah' refers to impulsive oaths made during moments of anger, which require repentance and regret.
